Material Rule: No later mortar/stone finish in AD30 materials.
Geometry Rule: Repairs, blocking walls, reused portals, later roofs and enclosure changes are reference-only.

Material Rule: Separate later carved stone, mortar, vault and façade fabrics.
Primary Evidence: Southern Wall archaeology and architectural studies
Geometry Rule: Current Triple Gate three-arch façade and Umayyad structures treated as later reference unless a surviving Herodian component is independently identified.
Notes: Critical to avoid using visible Triple Gate façade as Herodian original.

Material Rule: Weathering/wear may be applied procedurally but must not fabricate later masonry replacement.
Period: Early Roman, Temple in active use
Geometry Rule: Represents wear, repairs and operational elements demonstrably plausible by AD30 without importing post-70 fabric.
Notes: Separate from original construction date when useful for surface aging.

Material Rule: Use Herodian-period fabric records only; later repairs remain separate objects.
Primary Evidence: Josephus; Middot; Temple Mount archaeology; Herodian construction remains
Geometry Rule: Primary master geometry for retaining walls, gates, platform, courts, sanctuary and contemporary substructure where evidence supports.
Date Range: late 1st c BCE–early 1st c CE; intended AD30 standing state
Notes: This is the target visual/structural state.

Material Rule: Do not recolor/rework earlier masonry as Herodian drafted ashlar.
Geometry Rule: Preserve only where bedrock, earlier wall/core or reused structural line demonstrably constrains Herodian construction.
Date Range: before Herod's major Temple Mount expansion
Notes: 500-cubit core may intersect this phase as reconstruction hypothesis.

Material Rule: Mortared fieldstone and Byzantine hydraulic plasters must not overwrite Herodian fabric unless reused material is explicitly isolated.
Geometry Rule: Walls, fills, pavements and repairs of these phases must remain comparison layers.
Notes: IAA A-9477 Strata 2–3 provide local examples.

Material Rule: Do not use burned/collapse weathering as default AD30 surface.
Geometry Rule: Collapsed stones/destruction fills may be reference/context only, never part of standing AD30 geometry.
Notes: Useful for identifying displaced Herodian blocks, not reconstructing standing placement without proof.

Material Rule: Never bake modern conservation surface into historical texture.
Geometry Rule: Excavation tunnels, supports, restorations, concrete and reconstructed steps are survey/reference geometry only.
Notes: Example: A-9477 modern underground excavation tunnel dimensions are NOT ancient tunnel dimensions.
